name: Hester Biosciences Ltd
title: Hester Biosciences Ltd - 524669 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 standalone growth of 14% and 88% PAT rise, but consolidated revenue fell 8% on Nepal and Africa, and management gave no numeric guidance; utilisation is about 60-65%, so no capacity discipline signal.

utilisation.quote: at an average, you can say we have around 65% utilization, and that's about it.

triggers.quote: our capacity utilization over here at the plant, it is at around 60% to 65%

red_flags.quote: Receivables are a little higher. Sometimes this is due to seasonal issues and all.

summary.headline: Hester Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 88% and gross margin up to 78%, while consolidated revenue fell 8% on Nepal and Africa weakness.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 14% YoY and EBITDA rose 95%, with gross margin improving from 69% to 78% on product mix and operational efficiencies. Consolidated revenue declined 8%, mainly on lower Nepal and Africa revenues. Consolidated profit included an exceptional gain from the Gates Foundation amendment that cut the Hester Africa soft loan from USD 12 million to USD 5 million, waived accrued interest and made the loan interest-free. Poultry grew 48% on institutional business and deeper penetration, while Animal Healthcare was held back by delayed government immunisation programmes (PPR, Lumpy Skin Disease / Goat Pox).

financial_highlights.metric: Hester Africa Gates Foundation soft loan
financial_highlights.value: Reduced from USD 12 million to USD 5 million, interest-free
financial_highlights.change: Exceptional accounting gain in consolidated profit

segments.name: Poultry Healthcare Division
segments.commentary: Grew 48% YoY on higher institutional business and deeper market penetration. Management said the low pathogenic avian influenza vaccine, approved in March 2026, contributed to the jump. Management also cited early traction in poultry health products (feed supplements, disinfectants).

segments.name: Animal Healthcare Division
segments.commentary: Impacted by timing of government immunisation programmes (PPR eradication, Lumpy Skin Disease Control Initiative, Goat Pox vaccine supply). Management described this as timing-related rather than a demand issue.

segments.name: International (Nepal and Africa)
segments.commentary: Revenues were low in the quarter and drove the consolidated decline. Management said strategic direction is unchanged, focused on registration, market development and commercial presence.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: Emerging, not reported separately and included within animal health. Product categories are antibiotics, anti-parasites and grooming products sold under the Hester brand.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give directional guidance on Africa demand or when it would turn profitable, describing the region as a formative period.
Management said the delayed government vaccine tender business is expected to come through in the next quarter.
No numerical guidance was given on revenue, margins or capacity utilisation targets.
Management said it is not providing guidance on the capacity utilisation trajectory.
capex_capacity: Average plant capacity utilisation is around 60% to 65%, covering the whole manufacturing set-up (poultry, large animal, and the newly added fill-and-finish and BSL3 facilities).
New fill-and-finish and BSL3 facilities came online a couple of quarters ago. Management did not give a utilisation figure for these specifically.
Fixed assets rose by around Rs. 200 crore in FY26 (per analyst), with the new facilities cited as the driver. Management did not dispute the figure.
Pipeline products under development at the new facilities were not disclosed. Recombinant Brucella vaccine development is said to be progressing on timeline.
Regulatory dossiers were submitted in animal health during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Poultry growth came mainly from higher market share and deeper penetration; management said vaccine prices have only marginally increased.
Government tender timing caused animal vaccine sales to slip from Q1, with management expecting them to come in the next quarter.
Management said the poultry vaccine business is shared across India, Nepal and Africa; poultry exports from India are part of the consolidated poultry top line.
Management said the poultry distribution network is the same for vaccines and health products, with cross-selling of feed supplements and medicines under way.
Management said there was no material impact on the industry from the H5N1 culling compensation delay.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ministry's recent decision on HPAI vaccine imports for testing, and how does Hester benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Gandhi said it is premature to comment: the government still has to decide whether the vaccine will be imported or made in India.

qa_highlights.question: How does the poultry business's sharp growth compare with its historical track record? Is it cyclical or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said the division pushed sales where opportunities arose, while animal health sales slipped due to tender delays. No value or volume split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation, and can sales grow without new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said average utilisation is about 60% to 65%, but noted that this is subjective given the mix of batch sizes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the step-up in poultry revenue from about Rs. 45-48 crore to over Rs. 60 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi attributed it to better placement and more aggressive market penetration, with price increases contributing little.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash conversion weak, given that receivables are higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said operating cash flow is positive and conversion has improved. Rajiv Gandhi said higher receivables are seasonal and not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Africa operation's slow scale-up a natural gestation period or a tendering problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said it is a formative period in a new continent with economic and political strain. He declined to give directional guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Africa tax holiday timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said the tax-free status runs until 2030.

risks_watch: Africa and Nepal revenue weakness, with no profitability timeline given and geopolitical constraints acknowledged by management.
Animal Healthcare dependence on government tender timing, with the next quarter expected to see catch-up sales.
Receivables rising, which management attributes to seasonality. Analysts questioned cash conversion.
Low utilisation (about 65%) despite the recent fill-and-finish and BSL3 capacity additions, with fixed assets up about Rs. 200 crore in FY26.
Regulatory and policy uncertainty on HPAI vaccine import or domestic manufacturing pathway.
Gates Foundation loan reduction, which boosted consolidated profit through a one-time exceptional gain rather than operations.
summary.management_tone: Confident on standalone profitability and poultry growth, but evasive on Africa, Nepal, pet vaccines, utilisation numbers, pipeline products and HPAI policy, repeatedly declining to quantify or guide. Management dismissed the receivables and cash conversion concern as seasonal.
key_quotes: As we have consistently maintained, this remains a timing-related issue rather than a reflection of any underlying demand issue.
We would not want to get into any directional guidance or anything.

adds.what: New fill-and-finish and BSL3 facilities (online for a couple of quarters; capex not stated)

growth.why: No numerical guidance was given; management declined Africa and utilisation outlooks and cited only a delayed government vaccine tender expected next quarter, with poultry share gains and a new low-path avian influenza vaccine driving the 48% poultry jump against 65% utilisation.
